govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CommitteeForAct: This Fifth Estate item — Quarterly Journal of the Fifth Estate, Vol. 2, Issue 2 — is a counterculture journal issue. The Fifth Estate covered the underground. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agnus-dei: This 1913 reference article on the Agnus Dei — the blessed wax discs of papal Rome. Herbert Thurston describes their making and lore. Popes blessed them in holy years. The faithful wore them for protection. A sacramental of old devotion. Their impressions show the paschal lamb.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-allesandro-ga: This 1913 reference article on Alessandro Galilei — the Florentine architect of the Lateran facade. Thomas Poole praises his Roman work. His front crowns St. John Lateran. Florence trained his classic taste. An architect of the late Baroque. His Corsini chapel graces the Lateran.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancilla-dei: A 1913 entry on Ancilla Dei — the handmaid of God, the nun's proud title. Maurice Hassett explains its ancient use. The virgins signed it on their tombs. Humility became a name of honor. The Church's lowliest title. Its letters mark the nuns' seals.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-auctorem-fide: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Auctorem Fidei — Pius VI's bull against the Synod of Pistoia. Michael O'Riordan explains its eighty-five censures. The Jansenist decrees were condemned. The Church guarded its ancient discipline. The bull that crushed the synod. Its Latin is the curia's finest.
